name: @civitai/app-sdk
description: OAuth + PKCE, encrypted-cookie sessions, scopes, and orchestrator helpers for building third-party Civitai apps.

purpose (this package ships into sandboxed browser iframes and every app
inherits its install graph), and @civitai/client has no types-only entry
point -- it ships .d.ts beside .js in one package with a real runtime
(@hey-api/client-fetch, rfc6902, tslib). Optional-peer keeps that graph
out of every app that does not ask for the step types, and keeps the

comment-peerDependencies-ajv-vite: ajv and vite are OPTIONAL peers of the NODE-ONLY subpaths added when #330
`dependencies` stays EMPTY for the same reason it always has: this package
ships into sandboxed browser iframes and every app inherits its install
graph. A build-time JSON-Schema engine has no business in that graph, so
ajv is a peer a scaffold opts into: `pnpm add -D ajv`.
ajv: a VALUE import (`ajv/dist/2020.js`, the draft 2020-12 entry — the
canonical schema declares $schema draft/2020-12, so the default `ajv`
entry point would refuse to compile it). FLOOR ^8.17.1: `ajv/dist/2020`
has existed since 8.6.0, but 8.17.x is what this repo builds and tests
against, and 8.x is a single major so the caret admits every later 8.
vite: TYPES ONLY (`import type { Plugin }`). Nothing is value-imported, so
there is no module-evaluation failure mode -- only a typecheck one. The
`./vite` reads) has been stable across all of them; this repo builds and
tests against vite 8, which is what every scaffold pins.
